summary: Erection of a state fire observation tower on Hulbert Hill, Langlade County, began in 1928; the inventory lists it as gone.

facts.design: State fire observation tower; the 1928 report gave a planned height of 73 feet (22 m).
facts.status_note: The inventory lists it as gone. No source found gives a removal date or describes the site now.

events.note: Erection reported started in July 1928. No source found gives a completion date.

evidence.supports: Erection of a second state tower started on Hulbert Hill, two and a half miles north of Bryant
evidence.quote: Erection of a second state fire observation tower in Langlade county has been started on Hulbert hill, two and one-half miles north of Bryant.

evidence.supports: Planned height of 73 feet and wide view of the central county
evidence.quote: It will be 73 feet high and command a wide view of the central part of the county.

evidence.supports: First county state tower on Nine Mile Hill
evidence.quote: The first tower is located on Nine Mile hill in the eastern part of the county.

evidence.supports: Attribution of the report to the Stevens Point Daily Journal
evidence.quote: in Oneida county." (Stevens Point Daily Journal)

evidence.supports: Inventory lists Bryant (Hulbert Hill), Langlade County, as a tower now gone

sources.title: Wisconsin Forest Lookouts (transcribes the Stevens Point Daily Journal, July 27, 1928)

notes_for_editor: The only build evidence is one 1928 newspaper item, read through a hobby site's transcription (Central US Lookouts), not the newspaper page. It says erection had started, not that the tower was finished. No source found gives completion, staffing, fires, removal or the site today. Access is unknown, so no access fact is recorded. The 73 ft figure is the planned height from 1928. The 2.5 miles north of Bryant claim was not checked against the coordinates. A Stevens Point Daily Journal page or a Langlade County Historical Society record would firm up the build date.
